newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: MMI seeks to raise Australian market share.
newsitem.headline: MMI seeks to raise Australian market share.

text.p: MMI Ltd said on Tuesday it would restructure its Australian operations in an attempt to win a greater share of the business insurance market, in particular workers compensation and general insurance.
Managing director Pieter Franzen said the company aimed to increase its share of the workers compensation market to about 27.5 percent from 25 percent at the moment.
Franzen told Reuters that this line of business had a national value of about A$3 billion and the company's share was A$820 million.
This section of the market was only moderately profitable for MMI, which reports its 1996/97 (June-July) results in a few weeks.
"But I think that our ability to service this business more effectively may well help our profitability," he said.
MMI had about seven percent of the A$4 billion general insurance market and was seeking to raise this to 10 percent in three years.
The restructuring was aimed at the company's brokered-insurance operations, he said, with a strong emphasis on new technology, staff training, and cost savings.
Franzen said the company, which is 38 perent owned by Allianz AG, would seek to retrain and redeploy staff rather than impose retrenchments.
